models.name: BitNet b1.58 2B4T
models.summary: Microsoft Research's native 1-bit LLM at 2B scale: ternary {-1, 0, +1} weights and 8-bit activations, trained from scratch with the quantization scheme (not post-training quantized) on 4T tokens. The model card is explicit that the standard `transformers` path gives none of the claimed efficiency -- the packed weights only pay off under `bitnet.cpp`'s BitLinear kernels. Two variants registered here: the packed safetensors repo (source weights) and the official GGUF (`bitnet.cpp` CPU inference).

variants.name: BitNet b1.58 2B4T (packed 1.58-bit weights)

download.note: Whole repo at the pinned commit: the packed ternary model.safetensors (1,178,623,988 bytes) plus tokenizer and config files. Hub API listed no GGUF sibling in this repo -- the GGUF build is a separate repo, registered as this model's other variant.

working_set.note: Model card's own comparison table states "Memory (Non-emb): 0.4GB" for BitNet b1.58 2B under bitnet.cpp -- a publisher claim, not a SpacePilot measurement. The same table claims 29ms CPU decode latency and 0.028J estimated energy per generation, both declared, not measured here.

variants.notes:
Official inference code: https://github.com/microsoft/BitNet (bitnet.cpp), MIT licence, commit 0b341e582afbf9e1011f24744b554c96a3477eb5 on main checked 2026-09-10 (that repo's README documents CPU kernels for x86/ARM plus a GPU kernel added 2026-05-20; NPU support is listed as "coming next", not shipped). Runtime recipe: spacepilot/registry/runtimes/bitnet-cpp.yaml, pinned to the same commit -- no PyPI wheel, source-tree CMake build; that recipe's notes carry the full build/run sequence and why it was recorded rather than run this pass.
Model card, verbatim warning (checked 2026-09-10): "Please do NOT expect performance efficiency gains (in terms of speed, latency, or energy consumption) when using this model with the standard transformers library, even with the required fork ... For achieving the efficiency benefits demonstrated in the technical paper, you MUST use the dedicated C++ implementation: bitnet.cpp." So this `-packed` variant is the source-of-truth weights; the GGUF variant below is the one bitnet.cpp actually reads efficiently.
Card claims a 54.19 average across ARC-Challenge/Easy, OpenbookQA, BoolQ, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, CommonsenseQA, TruthfulQA, TriviaQA, MMLU, HumanEval+, GSM8K, MATH-500, IFEval and MT-bench against similarly-sized full-precision open models (Qwen2.5-1.5B's 55.23 is the only one that beats it) -- declared by the publisher, not reproduced by SpacePilot.
Status: unflown. Executor-candidate role for the router bench and the L2R typed tasks, per the ternary/1.58-bit registration brief (2026-09-10).

Prerouter: a trained head predicts expert routing one step ahead so expert loads overlap the forward pass instead of stalling it, claimed up to +59% decode throughput. The Hub listing also tags this repo `cuda`, but the Q2_0 kernel README quoted above only documents CPU and Metal support -- `backends` here follows the README over the tag, so CUDA is left out rather than asserted on a tag alone.

Not attempted this pass -- a default llama.cpp CMake configure enables the Metal backend on Apple Silicon by itself, a full build, not a small or quick one; see the recipe's own notes for the build command.
